guideTabTitle: How to Submit a Project & Rate Entries
guideTabSubtitle: All submissions undergo automated validation. Below are the required title prefixes, [rating](0-100) scoring rules, and link standards.
guidePrefixTitle: Required GitHub Submission Title Format (Prefix + Name)
guidePrefixDesc: When creating an Issue or Pull Request, the submission title must start with the lowercase project type followed by a colon:
guideRule1Desc: Icons must be .svg, .png, or .jpg URLs. Screenshots must be direct .png or .jpg URLs (or left empty if none).
guideRule2Title: 2. Validated Country (or Europa, USA, Asia, Africa) & Source Host
guideRule2Desc: Enter a valid country or choose Europa, USA, Asia, or Africa. Open source links are verified against the selected platform (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, SourceForge, Gitee, CNB), or marked Proprietary.
guideRule3Title: 3. Website Link or Project Fallback URL
guideRule3Desc: Every project links to its official website, or automatically falls back to its repository or related project page.
guideRule4Desc: You can provide descriptions in multiple languages. Users rate projects from 0 to 100 by ending their Issue comment with [rating](0-100).
submitTabSubtitle: Watch the animated workflow tutorial below, validate your project data in real time, and proceed to GitHub.
animTitle: Workflow Animation: From Submission to Bot Publication
animStep1Text: Select the prefix (launcher:, modpack:, mod:, client:, project:) and write descriptions in one or multiple languages.
animStep2Text: Checks real country (or Europa/USA/Asia/Africa), exact repository domain match (e.g. github.com), and .svg/.png/.jpg image formats.
animStep3Text: Click the proceed button — GitHub opens with your pre-validated Issue or Pull Request ready to submit.
animStep4Text: The GitHub bot verifies the submission, opens the review thread, and parses [rating](0-100) scores.
